newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran seizes 11 tonnes of drugs in one month.
newsitem.headline: Iran seizes 11 tonnes of drugs in one month.

text.p: Iranian police have seized more than 11 tonnes (24,255 lb) of narcotics in one month, the official news agency IRNA said on Wednesday.
It said the haul was confiscated in 1,504 operations from 2,704 drug traffickers in the month to July 22.
Quoting a police official, IRNA said the drugs included 9,737 kg (21,470 lb) of opium, 537 kg (1,184 lb) of hashish and 61 kg (134 lb) of heroin.
Iran is a key transit route for drugs, mostly opium from which heroin is made, being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan -- the so-called "Golden Crescent."
Tehran has said police seized 175 tonnes of drugs in the Iranian year which ended on March 20.
More than 1,000 people have been executed in Iran since a 1989 law took effect imposing the death sentence for possession of five kg (11 lb) of opium or 30 grams (just over one ounce) of heroin.
Iranian newspapers said on Sunday Tehran planned to introduce tough legislation calling for stiffer punishment for drug smugglers. They did not give details of the new penalties.
